title: Personal Golden Signals Rollup
dataSources: Daily life scores (`lifescore:daily`), personal SLO status (`personalslo:status`), cross-signal correlations (`correlation:pair`), plus every other `index=personal` sourcetype as input.
app: The meta layer — correlating every `index=personal` feed (sleep, activity, mood, weather, spend, productivity, home telemetry) into daily life scores, personal SLOs, and cross-signal anomaly detection, all computed in Splunk.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=personalslo:status
| stats avg(latency_score) as latency, avg(error_budget_pct) as error_budget, avg(saturation_pct) as saturation, avg(availability_pct) as availability by service
| sort service
description: Rolls up a personal version of the golden signals across the services and habits you care about most.
value: Treating life systems like services can sound silly, but it is a sharp way to see overload, fragility, and missed expectations.
implementation: Publish personal-SLO status events into `index=personal`; summarize the key golden-signal metrics per service.
visualization: Service table of latency, error-budget, saturation, and availability metrics.
grandmaExplanation: It watches the basic health signals for the parts of life you track, so overload and drift stand out earlier.
